_readme: THE CONFIG SEAM. Everything project-specific the harness knows lives in this file, and the
harness code requires nothing from the repo it grades. That is the whole design move: the
mechanism is general, this file is the project.
AN ABSENT OR MALFORMED CONFIG IS A HARD STOP, never a default. A harness that invents its own
gate list when it cannot read one prints a green verdict about a suite nobody agreed to, and
that figure is the one people then trust. scripts/harness/config.js has no default `gates`
array and never may.
`artifacts` has no `_readme` of its own because it is an array. It is the REPRODUCIBLE-BUILD
check: every path (or glob) listed is hashed before the suite and after it, and the gate is
red unless each committed artifact is byte-identical to what this source produces. The check
exists for repos where the committed bundle IS the deploy, so a source edit committed without
a rebuild ships code no gate ever rendered while every other gate stays green.
THIS repo builds no bundles, so the list is empty — and an empty list DECLARES ITSELF. The
check prints `not applicable, 0 artifacts graded` and reports skipped=1; it never passes
silently, because pass-by-absence is the exact failure the gate protocol exists to end. A skip
is red unless the CALLER tolerates it, so this repo's own green invocation is:
node scripts/harness/gates.js --check --allow-skip reproducible-build=1
The decision to tolerate it is in the invocation, where it is visible, and not in the gate's
own opinion of its environment.
The schema beside this file documents every key. `node scripts/harness/config.js` prints the
resolved config, defaults merged in, which is how you find out what the harness thinks it is
grading before it grades it.
What this repo is called in every report, and where its prose lives.
name        labels the repo in gate output and in generated docs.
docsRoot    the root of the doc contract: frontmatter, line caps, the generated index.
tracksDir   where a track folder goes (README.md, plan.md, traps.md, handoff.md, research/).
Both paths must stay inside the repo — an absolute path or a `..` is rejected, because a doc
linter pointed outside the tree grades files no commit can fix.
sourceBranch  OPTIONAL and unset here on purpose. It is the branch every other branch's
harness is compared against (scripts/harness/branch-sync.js). Unset, the script
DETECTS it — the remote's published head, then the first of main, master, trunk,
default that exists — and says which it used, so this repo follows whatever its
default branch is called. State it only where detection would be wrong.
project.name: agent-harness

_readme: THE GATE REGISTRY, in run order. Each entry is a command whose LAST stdout line is exactly
`GATE <name> pass=<n> fail=<n> skipped=<n>`. pass+fail+skipped is the TOTAL, and the total
is the load-bearing part: comparing only `pass` cannot tell a green run from a run where
checks VANISHED. A gate that emits no GATE line is a hard failure — silence is not success.
name      kebab-case. It is the token in the GATE line, the key in the baseline, the
argument to --only, and the stem of gates.red.<name>.log.
command   a shell string. A leading bare `node` is re-pointed at the runtime the harness is
running under, so the suite is not graded by whichever node is on PATH.
adapter   only for a runner that prints its OWN summary and will not print ours:
`node-test` (reads node:test's pass/fail/skipped), `exit-code` (a tool whose
verdict IS its exit status). Omit it and the GATE line is parsed. An UNKNOWN
adapter is a hard error, never a fallback — a typo would otherwise read as a gate
that crashed before its verdict and send the reader to the wrong file.
optional  true means an ABSENT TOOL declares a skip instead of a fail. It does NOT mean the
gate is optional: a tool that is present and unhappy still fails. The skip is then
red unless the caller passes --allow-skip <name>=1.
gateLine  the name the command actually prints, when it differs from `name` — which is how
one script can be gated twice under two different environments.
WITHOUT THIS SECTION there is no suite, and the harness stops rather than guessing one.
Gates run in declaration order, because a repo's gates are not independent: a build gate has
to run before the check that grades what it produced.
THE `test` COMMAND BELOW IS `node --test` WITH NO PATH, and that was measured on both sides
of Node 21. A quoted glob is not understood before it (exit, `Could not find`), and a bare
directory is read as a module from it on (one failing test). With no path every supported
version finds the same *.test.js files, which is what `engines: >=20` needs to be true.
gates.name: test

_readme: THE RUN-MODE SCRIPTS. `mode`, `effects` and `peers` each grade the SCRIPT, by its own
self-test: one check, the exit status. They say the verdict logic still holds. They do NOT
say a mode is in force, that any effects ledger is clean, or that a claim hook is wired:
mode.js is registered on no hook event, there is no ledger in this repo to grade, and the
peers hook is not installed.
`carveouts` is the one that grades the TREE: the waivers in the git index, per kind,
against the census in scripts/harness/carveouts.baseline.json. It is a count of MENTIONS,
so a doc or test edit that spells a waiver moves it and reds the gate until the census is
re-recorded on a clean tree: node scripts/harness/carveouts.js --accept
--i-know-the-tree-is-clean. Reason-less waivers may fall and never rise.
gates.name: mode

_readme: THE SECRET-FILE STANCE, read by the PreToolUse env guard. The default is DENY-ALL: a matched
path is refused for reading, writing and shelling out to, whatever the tool.
guarded        glob-ish patterns for the files no agent may open.
openCarveOuts  the explicit, DATED exceptions. Each is { path, why, until } and the `until`
is required — an undated carve-out is permanent by accident. Every open
carve-out is reported at SessionStart until it is removed, so the exception is
something you keep seeing rather than something you forget.
WITHOUT THIS SECTION the guard has no deny list, and a credential file is one `cat` away from
a transcript that leaves the machine.
WHERE WORKING FILES ARE ALLOWED TO LIVE, read by the commit-hygiene check and the gate that
reports it.
workDirs   the directories a working file belongs in. Anything else at the top level is a
stray.
rootAllow  the files that legitimately sit at the repo root. Everything not on this list is
refused there.
WITHOUT THIS SECTION the root accumulates scratch files, and the first casualty is this
harness's own state: gates.json and gates.baseline.json live beside their script precisely
because a root-level baseline needed a hygiene waiver on every run, and a gate you waive
routinely is a gate you have switched off.
THE DOC CONTRACT'S HARD LIMITS, read by the doc linter.
caps        line ceilings. `AGENTS.md` is the always-on policy file, so its ceiling is the
tightest; `CLAUDE.md` is the stub that imports it, capped at the size of a
pointer; `subtreeAgentsMd` is a per-directory AGENTS.md (and the stub beside it);
`default` applies to every other doc. Every value must be a POSITIVE INTEGER — a
cap of 0 is not `no cap`, it is a cap nothing can satisfy, and a float compares
strangely. Both are typos; neither is a policy.
exemptDirs  the directories where frozen evidence lives. Archived tracks and dated audits are
frozen on purpose, so a linter that rewrote them to fit a cap would be editing the
record. Listing a directory here is more than a caps exemption: it also takes the
directory out of the no-gate-figure rule and the section-reference check, and
(unless it is the tracks directory) out of the arrow-block, dead-link and trap-id
rules too. So the tracks directory is deliberately NOT listed: a live tracker
quoting a stale total is the failure the figure rule exists for, and listing it
would switch that rule off exactly there. A research file needs no entry: it is
exempt by its own `kind`.
WITHOUT THIS SECTION there is no ceiling on always-on context, and the file every session
loads grows until it crowds out the work.
THE ALWAYS-ON CONTEXT BUDGET.
budgetFile  a HAND-WRITTEN fixture of per-file ceilings that no script ever rewrites. A
budget a tool can update is a budget that records whatever happened rather than
what was agreed, and the measurement then always agrees with itself.
WITHOUT THIS SECTION the context gate has no standard to grade against, and the cost of every
session's first token is nobody's business.
WHICH CODING AGENTS THIS REPO IS WIRED FOR.
enabled  tool ids, each a row of the registry, scripts/harness/tools.json. That file records
what each agent loads and what it can deny, with the evidence behind every row.
`node scripts/harness/tools.js --list` prints the ids; `--check` fails on an id here
that has no row.
WITHOUT THIS SECTION the list is the default, claude-code alone. A misspelled sub-key or a
value that is not an array is a hard stop, because a list that fell back to the default would
report a tool as enabled that this file never named.
